content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [["abcd","acbd","aacd"]]
content.outputFormat: Single line: JSON-serialised boolean return value

sampleTestCases.explanation: Every pair differs in two positions, so no pair differs by exactly one character.

content.problemStatement:
Given a list of strings `dict` where all the strings are of the same length.

Return `true` if there are 2 strings that only differ by 1 character in the same index, otherwise return `false`.

**Follow up:** Could you solve this problem in `O(n * m)` where `n` is the length of `dict` and `m` is the length of each string?

notes: Implement differByOne(dict) and return true when any two strings differ at exactly one index.
The trie approach is deterministic and avoids hash-collision concerns.
Because every word has the same length and words are unique, reaching a terminal node with exactly one mismatch identifies a different valid word.
solution.approach: Build a trie containing all input strings. For each word, traverse the trie while keeping at most two kinds of states: paths that still match every character seen so far, and paths that have already used exactly one mismatch. At each character, the zero-mismatch state can either follow the matching child or branch to any non-matching child, while a one-mismatch state must follow the matching child. If a terminal trie node is reached with exactly one mismatch, a valid pair exists.

better.complexity: O(n * m^2) time in the worst case because each masked string has length m, and O(n * m) space.
better.description: For each word and each position, replace that character with a marker such as `*` and store the resulting pattern in a hash set. Repeated patterns at the same position imply two words differ only at that position.

optimal.complexity: O(26 * n * m) = O(n * m) time and O(n * m) space, since the alphabet size is fixed at 26.
optimal.description: Insert all words into a trie. While searching each word, allow exactly one character transition to differ from the input word and then require exact matches for the remaining suffix. Any terminal node reached after exactly one mismatch proves that two words differ by one character.

bruteForce.complexity: O(n^2 * m) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
bruteForce.description: Compare every pair of strings and count character differences, stopping a comparison once more than one mismatch is found.

solution.timeComplexity: O(n * m) time, treating the lowercase alphabet size 26 as a constant.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(n * m) space in the worst case for the trie.

followUps: Can the problem be solved in O(n * m) using rolling hash?
Why does replacing one character with a marker lead to an O(n * m^2) approach?
How would the solution change if the alphabet were much larger?
What changes if duplicate strings were allowed?
